Package · MIT

ai-forms

Fill a form from prose, then refine it in conversation. Headless, so every app keeps its own look.

npm README & API Version history Source

Why it exists

People do not want to meet a form. They want to say what they need. Each product was about to build its own 'paste a paragraph, get fields' box, with its own prompt and its own way of being wrong.

How it works

A headless core turns prose into the fields a schema already allows, then lets the person correct them in conversation. A React hook and a route factory are optional. The form on the page stays the product's own.

Where it fits

It is how a sentence becomes a listing, an application, or an intake, on top of ai-kit. The studio's bet is that the interface to an economic life is closer to speech than to a spreadsheet.
